axial/propeller:
"Vz" — The horizontal component of the flight velocity, Vx: the aircraft's AIRSPEED. On a propeller the shaft is horizontal, so x runs ALONG THE SHAFT, and the engine adds the induced velocity to it to form Vx,total = Vx + vi.

THIS IS THE PROPELLER'S ADVANCE RATIO. The default unit Jx is the classic one of the propeller charts, Jx = V/(nD), built from the AXIAL airspeed -- the same Jx that propulsive efficiency uses, since thrust acts along the shaft.

Units offered: Jx, μx = Jx/π = Vx/(ΩR) (the same number in the rotor vocabulary, also written λx), and the dimensional speed Vx [m/s].

No angle is offered here, on purpose: an angle only splits the known component into the other one, and on a propeller the known component is this one. The angle lives in the cross-flow field above, measured from the shaft (αdisk).
axial/rotor:
"Vz" — The vertical component of the flight velocity, Vz. On a rotor the shaft is vertical, so z runs ALONG THE SHAFT: this is climb (positive) or descent (negative), and the engine adds the induced velocity to it to form Vz,total = Vz + vi.

Units offered: αrotor [deg], Vz [m/s], and the ratios μz = Vz/(ΩR) (also written λz) and Jz = Vz/(nD).

αrotor = atan2(Vz, Vx) is THE angle of rotor mode, measured FROM THE DISK PLANE: 0° is level forward flight, and it is POSITIVE when the flow arrives from below the disk. Propeller mode offers αdisk instead, measured from the shaft; each mode offers only its own angle, so there is never a doubt about which of the two a number is.

The angle lives in this field in both modes for one reason: an angle never fixes the scale of the velocity, it only splits the KNOWN component into the other one.
inplane/propeller:
"mu_x" — The cross-flow across the propeller shaft, Vz. Propeller axes: x is along the shaft, z is in the disk plane. In straight cruise Vz = 0 -- the aircraft's airspeed goes in the axial field below.

Units offered: Vz [m/s], αdisk [deg], μz = Vz/(ΩR), or Jz = Vz/(nD). Jz is the cross-flow, NOT the propeller advance ratio.

αdisk = atan2(Vz, Vx): 0° means the free stream is aligned with the shaft.
inplane/rotor:
"mu_x" — The horizontal component of the flight velocity, Vx. On a rotor the shaft is vertical, so x lies IN THE PLANE OF THE DISK: this is THE ADVANCE, the component that sweeps across the blades and makes the advancing and retreating sides differ.

Units offered: μx = Vx/(ΩR), Jx = Vx/(nD) = π·μx, and the dimensional speed Vx [m/s]. The vertical component Vz is the field below.

CH: H-force coefficient, in-plane drag-like force (+ aft)
CHi: Induced part of the H-force coefficient
CHp: Profile part of the H-force coefficient
CMy: Roll moment coefficient (+ roll toward the advancing side)
CPi: Induced part of the power coefficient
CPp: Profile (sectional drag) part of the power coefficient
CQ: Torque coefficient: C<sub>Q</sub> = Q / (ρ·A·(ΩR)²·R) — numerically equals C<sub>P</sub> for a rotor
CY: Side-force coefficient (+ toward the advancing side)
FM: Figure of Merit: ideal induced power / actual power. A static (V<sub>x</sub> = 0) figure of merit; in cruise the same formula can exceed 1 -- use η<sub>prop</sub> instead
Hp: Profile (sectional drag) part of the H-force [N]
J_x: Advance ratio along z in propeller form: J<sub>z</sub> = V<sub>z</sub>/(nD) = π·μ<sub>z</sub>. NOT the propeller advance ratio -- that one is J<sub>x</sub>, built from the airspeed along the shaft. This is the cross-flow, zero in straight cruise
J_z: Advance ratio along x in propeller form: J<sub>x</sub> = V<sub>x</sub>/(nD) = π·μ<sub>x</sub>. THIS IS THE J<sub>x</sub> of propeller charts, built from the airspeed along the shaft, and the one propulsive efficiency uses
Mx: Pitch moment about the hub [N·m], positive nose up
Mx_hub: Hub moment carried through the flap hinge or root spring [N·m], about the axis pointing to ψ=0: (N<sub>b</sub>/2)·I<sub>β</sub>Ω<sup>2</sup>(ν<sub>β</sub><sup>2</sup>−1)β<sub>1c</sub>. This structural path is absent on a rigid-blade run and dominates on hingeless rotors
Mx_total: Total tilting moment about the ψ=0 axis [N·m]: the aerodynamic moment M<sub>x</sub> plus the hub moment carried through the flap hinge or root spring M<sub>x,hub</sub>
My: Roll moment about the hub [N·m], positive toward the advancing side
My_hub: Hub moment carried through the flap hinge or root spring [N·m], about the ψ=90° axis: (N<sub>b</sub>/2)·I<sub>β</sub>Ω<sup>2</sup>(ν<sub>β</sub><sup>2</sup>−1)β<sub>1s</sub>
My_total: Total tilting moment about the ψ=90° axis [N·m]: the aerodynamic moment M<sub>y</sub> plus the hub moment carried through the flap hinge or root spring M<sub>y,hub</sub>
Power_i: Induced power [W]: the part spent creating the wake
Power_p: Profile power [W]: the part spent on blade sectional drag
Vi: Induced velocity [m/s], disk-averaged: the velocity the rotor adds along its own shaft. v<sub>i</sub> = λ<sub>i</sub>·(ΩR). It never changes axis with the mode -- only the letter naming that axis does
Vx: Free-stream component along z [m/s]. In propeller mode z is VERTICAL, across the shaft and in the plane of the disk: the cross-flow. ZERO in straight cruise; non-zero when the propeller flies at an angle to its axis
Vz: Free-stream component along x [m/s]. In propeller mode x is the SHAFT direction, so this is the aircraft's airspeed -- in straight cruise, the whole flight velocity. It is the FREE STREAM; the flow through the disk is V<sub>x,total</sub>
Vz_total: Total velocity along the shaft, through the disk [m/s]: V<sub>x,total</sub> = V<sub>x</sub> + v<sub>i</sub>, disk-averaged. The airspeed plus what the propeller adds. Written U<sub>P</sub> in the manual (Section 2.4.2)
Y: In-plane side force [N], positive toward the advancing side
alpha_disk_deg: DISK angle of attack [deg]: angle between the free stream and the SHAFT, α<sub>disk</sub> = 90 - α<sub>rotor</sub>. This is THE angle of propeller mode -- 0 in straight cruise (so a 2 deg misalignment reads '2'), and POSITIVE when the disk is tilted nose-up, i.e. the flow arrives from below. Its rotor-mode counterpart is α<sub>rotor</sub>, measured from the disk plane; each mode shows only its own
alpha_rotor_deg: ROTOR angle of attack [deg]: angle between the free stream and the DISK PLANE, α<sub>rotor</sub> = atan2(V<sub>z</sub>, V<sub>x</sub>). This is THE angle of rotor mode -- 0 in a helicopter's level forward flight, and POSITIVE when the flow arrives from below the disk. Its propeller-mode counterpart is α<sub>disk</sub>, measured from the shaft; the two are complementary and each mode shows only its own
beta_0_deg: Coning angle [deg]: the mean flap angle β<sub>0</sub>, the constant part of β(ψ) = β<sub>0</sub> + β<sub>1c</sub>cosψ + β<sub>1s</sub>sinψ. Positive with the blades up. It grows with thrust and falls with the square of the flap frequency ratio
beta_1c_deg: First cosine flap coefficient [deg]: the fore-aft 1/rev part of β(ψ). The longitudinal tip-path-plane tilt is its NEGATIVE (θ<sub>TPP,long</sub> = −β<sub>1c</sub>)
beta_1s_deg: First sine flap coefficient [deg]: the lateral 1/rev part of β(ψ). The lateral tip-path-plane tilt is its NEGATIVE (θ<sub>TPP,lat</sub> = −β<sub>1s</sub>)
beta_2c_deg: Cosine flap coefficient of harmonic 2 [deg], from the harmonic balance of β(ψ) = β<sub>0</sub> + Σ<sub>n</sub>[β<sub>nc</sub>cos(nψ) + β<sub>ns</sub>sin(nψ)]
beta_2s_deg: Sine flap coefficient of harmonic 2 [deg], from the harmonic balance of β(ψ).
beta_3c_deg: Cosine flap coefficient of harmonic 3 [deg], from the harmonic balance of β(ψ) = β<sub>0</sub> + Σ<sub>n</sub>[β<sub>nc</sub>cos(nψ) + β<sub>ns</sub>sin(nψ)]
beta_3s_deg: Sine flap coefficient of harmonic 3 [deg], from the harmonic balance of β(ψ).
beta_4c_deg: Cosine flap coefficient of harmonic 4 [deg], from the harmonic balance of β(ψ) = β<sub>0</sub> + Σ<sub>n</sub>[β<sub>nc</sub>cos(nψ) + β<sub>ns</sub>sin(nψ)]
beta_4s_deg: Sine flap coefficient of harmonic 4 [deg], from the harmonic balance of β(ψ).
beta_5c_deg: Cosine flap coefficient of harmonic 5 [deg], from the harmonic balance of β(ψ) = β<sub>0</sub> + Σ<sub>n</sub>[β<sub>nc</sub>cos(nψ) + β<sub>ns</sub>sin(nψ)]
beta_5s_deg: Sine flap coefficient of harmonic 5 [deg], from the harmonic balance of β(ψ).

cfg_pitt_peters_tol: Convergence tolerance for the Pitt-Peters outer loop
cfg_radial_flow_max_skew_deg: Maximum skew angle for the radial flow correction [deg]

cfg_relax_azimuth_factor: Relaxation factor applied near the azimuth crossing
cfg_relax_root_factor: Relaxation factor applied near the root
cfg_relax_root_threshold: Root threshold (r/R) below which relax_root_factor applies
cfg_relax_schedule: Whether adaptive relaxation scheduling is enabled
cfg_relax_tip_threshold: Tip threshold (r/R) above which relax_root_factor applies
cfg_reverse_flow_blend_factor: Blend sharpness factor for the reverse-flow model
cfg_reverse_flow_model: Model used for the reverse-flow region of the disk
cfg_rho: Air density configured [kg/m³] (before any per-condition override -- see rho_used)
cfg_rho_used: Air density actually used in this solve [kg/m³] (may differ from cfg_rho if overridden per condition)
cfg_stagnation_min_frac: Minimum converged fraction required to avoid the stagnation exit
cfg_stagnation_patience: Iterations of stagnation tolerated before declaring non-convergence
cfg_tol: Solver convergence tolerance on the true residual g(λ)-λ
cfg_use_compressibility: Whether the Prandtl-Glauert compressibility correction is applied
cfg_use_dynamic_stall: Whether dynamic stall correction is enabled
cfg_use_radial_flow_correction: Whether the radial (spanwise) flow correction is applied
cfg_use_rotational_augmentation: Whether rotational (Himmelskamp/Snel) lift augmentation is applied
collective_deg: Collective pitch [deg], added on top of the built-in blade twist
condition: Flight condition. Cases are numbered in the order they were run, so a row can be cited ("Case 3") and matched to the figure with the same label
convergence_pct: Percentage of mesh elements where the inflow fixed point converged [%]
cyclic_c_deg: Cyclic pitch, cosine harmonic [deg]: pitch that varies once per revolution as θ<sub>1c</sub>cosψ. With flap freedom it tilts the blade response fore-aft and is one of the two controls the zero-flapping trim solves
cyclic_s_deg: Cyclic pitch, sine harmonic [deg]: pitch that varies once per revolution as θ<sub>1s</sub>sinψ. Together with the cosine harmonic it forms the pair the trim solves
dynamic_stall_periodic_residual: Largest change of the Oye separation function between the last two marched revolutions. Near zero means the time march reached a periodic regime; a value above 1e-3 means the transient had NOT decayed and more revolutions are needed (EN-9). Only reported by the 'time_march' dynamic-stall method
dynamic_stall_revolutions: Revolutions marched by the 'time_march' dynamic-stall method, echoed beside its periodic residual (EN-9)
eta_prop: Propulsive efficiency: η = T·V<sub>x</sub>/P = J<sub>x</sub>·C<sub>T,prop</sub>/C<sub>P,prop</sub>. Built from the airspeed ALONG THE SHAFT, since thrust acts there; meaningful with V<sub>x</sub> > 0
flap_inertia_kg_m2: Resolved flap inertia of one blade about its hinge [kg·m²], whichever inertia source was chosen. It normalizes the flap moment in the harmonic balance
inflow_coupling: How the inflow field is coupled across elements (local = per element, global = few global DOF)
lambda_i: Induced inflow ratio: λ<sub>i</sub> = v<sub>i</sub>/(ΩR), the unknown solved by the BEMT fixed point. Area-weighted mean over the meshed span (root cutout to tip), not the whole geometric disk
lambda_total: Total inflow ratio along the shaft: λ<sub>total</sub> = λ<sub>i</sub> + λ<sub>x</sub> -- the free-stream part plus the induced part. Its dimensional counterpart is V<sub>x,total</sub> = λ<sub>total</sub>·(ΩR)
lambda_z: Inflow ratio along x, from the free stream alone: λ<sub>x</sub> = V<sub>x</sub>/(ΩR). In propeller mode x is the shaft, so this is the axial inflow -- an input datum, known before any aerodynamics. THE SAME NUMBER as μ<sub>x</sub>, in the inflow vocabulary
lock_number: Lock number: γ = ρ·a·c<sub>ref</sub>·R<sup>4</sup>/I<sub>β</sub>, the ratio of aerodynamic to inertial blade response, built from the chord at r/R = 0.75. It sets how strongly the air moves the blade
mean_iter: Mean number of solver iterations per mesh element
mu_x: Advance ratio along z: μ<sub>z</sub> = V<sub>z</sub>/(ΩR), the cross-flow normalized by tip speed. This is the component that varies with azimuth and makes one side of the disk see more speed than the other. Zero in straight cruise
mu_z: Advance ratio along x: μ<sub>x</sub> = V<sub>x</sub>/(ΩR), the airspeed normalized by tip speed. THE SAME NUMBER as λ<sub>x</sub>, in the advance-ratio vocabulary
nu_beta: Flap frequency ratio: ν<sub>β</sub><sup>2</sup> = 1 + (3/2)·e/(1−e) + K<sub>β</sub>/(I<sub>β</sub>Ω<sup>2</sup>). How far the first flap mode sits above the rotor rotation. An articulated rotor has exactly 1, which is why its first harmonic resonates
nu_zeta: Lead-lag frequency ratio: ν<sub>ζ</sub><sup>2</sup> = (3/2)·e/(1−e) + K<sub>ζ</sub>/(I<sub>ζ</sub>Ω<sup>2</sup>). No leading 1: the lag freedom gets no restoring term from the thrust
rotor_rpm: Engine echo of the rotational speed built into the Rotor object [rev/min]. Same quantity as RPM; it is shown as a separate column only in the (abnormal) case where the two disagree
rpm: Rotational speed of the rotor for this condition [rev/min] -- the value the solver actually ran with. Same quantity as RPM<sub>rotor</sub> (the engine's own echo of it), which is therefore hidden from the table whenever the two agree
solver: Fixed-point solver used for the inflow equation
tpp_tilt_lat_deg: Lateral tip-path-plane tilt [deg]: how far the disk tilts sideways under flapping, θ<sub>TPP,lat</sub> = −β<sub>1s</sub>. On a rotor it reflects the classic response to the advancing/retreating load asymmetry
tpp_tilt_long_deg: Longitudinal tip-path-plane tilt [deg]: how far the disk tilts fore-aft under flapping, θ<sub>TPP,long</sub> = −β<sub>1c</sub>. Negative usually means the disk blows back relative to the shaft
zeta_0_deg: Mean lead-lag angle [deg]: the constant part of ζ(ψ). Positive against the direction of rotation

flap_inertia_kg_m2: Resolved flap inertia of one blade about its hinge [kg·m²], whichever inertia source was chosen. It normalizes the flap moment in the harmonic balance
inflow_coupling: How the inflow field is coupled across elements (local = per element, global = few global DOF)
lambda_i: Induced inflow ratio: λ<sub>i</sub> = v<sub>i</sub>/(ΩR), the unknown solved by the BEMT fixed point. Area-weighted mean over the meshed span (root cutout to tip), not the whole geometric disk
lambda_total: Total inflow ratio along the shaft: λ<sub>total</sub> = λ<sub>i</sub> + λ<sub>z</sub> -- the free-stream part plus the induced part. Its dimensional counterpart is V<sub>z,total</sub> = λ<sub>total</sub>·(ΩR)
lambda_z: Inflow ratio along z, from the free stream alone: λ<sub>z</sub> = V<sub>z</sub>/(ΩR). In rotor mode z is the shaft, so this is the climb inflow -- an input datum, known before any aerodynamics. THE SAME NUMBER as μ<sub>z</sub>, in the inflow vocabulary instead of the advance-ratio one
lock_number: Lock number: γ = ρ·a·c<sub>ref</sub>·R<sup>4</sup>/I<sub>β</sub>, the ratio of aerodynamic to inertial blade response, built from the chord at r/R = 0.75. It sets how strongly the air moves the blade
mean_iter: Mean number of solver iterations per mesh element
mu_x: Advance ratio along x: μ<sub>x</sub> = V<sub>x</sub>/(ΩR). In rotor mode x is the IN-PLANE direction, so this is the classic forward-flight advance ratio -- the component that sweeps across the blades and makes the advancing and retreating sides differ
mu_z: Advance ratio along z: μ<sub>z</sub> = V<sub>z</sub>/(ΩR). In rotor mode z is the SHAFT direction, so this is climb (positive) or descent (negative). Same number as λ<sub>z</sub>, written in the advance-ratio vocabulary instead of the inflow one
nu_beta: Flap frequency ratio: ν<sub>β</sub><sup>2</sup> = 1 + (3/2)·e/(1−e) + K<sub>β</sub>/(I<sub>β</sub>Ω<sup>2</sup>). How far the first flap mode sits above the rotor rotation. An articulated rotor has exactly 1, which is why its first harmonic resonates
nu_zeta: Lead-lag frequency ratio: ν<sub>ζ</sub><sup>2</sup> = (3/2)·e/(1−e) + K<sub>ζ</sub>/(I<sub>ζ</sub>Ω<sup>2</sup>). No leading 1: the lag freedom gets no restoring term from the thrust
rotor_rpm: Engine echo of the rotational speed built into the Rotor object [rev/min]. Same quantity as RPM; it is shown as a separate column only in the (abnormal) case where the two disagree
rpm: Rotational speed of the rotor for this condition [rev/min] -- the value the solver actually ran with. Same quantity as RPM<sub>rotor</sub> (the engine's own echo of it), which is therefore hidden from the table whenever the two agree
solver: Fixed-point solver used for the inflow equation
tpp_tilt_lat_deg: Lateral tip-path-plane tilt [deg]: how far the disk tilts sideways under flapping, θ<sub>TPP,lat</sub> = −β<sub>1s</sub>. On a rotor it reflects the classic response to the advancing/retreating load asymmetry
tpp_tilt_long_deg: Longitudinal tip-path-plane tilt [deg]: how far the disk tilts fore-aft under flapping, θ<sub>TPP,long</sub> = −β<sub>1c</sub>. Negative usually means the disk blows back relative to the shaft
zeta_0_deg: Mean lead-lag angle [deg]: the constant part of ζ(ψ). Positive against the direction of rotation
